terms.gloss: drive out or away; rout (an enemy)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; the place with the ablative alone or with ex, dē or ab
evidence: Cic. Pis. 23: cum virī bonī lapidibus ē forō pellerentur (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 1.40: sē patriō rēgnō pulsōs esse (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is to strike or beat: terram pede pellere, to stamp the ground (Lucr. 5.1402, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Pis. 16: mē domō meā expulistis (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: cum virī bonī lapidibus ē forō pellerentur
phrases.english: when good men were being driven from the forum with stones
you drove me out of my own house

sources: Lewis & Short: pello · Lewis & Short: expello
